title: He didn’t kiss Jesus…
paragraphs:
He didn’t kiss Jesus…
He denied Him.

And somehow…
that feels closer to home.

Thirty pieces of silver.
A public scandal.
A kiss in the dark.

The kind that says,
“I’m not like Judas…”
Peter didn’t plan to betray Jesus.
“Even if all fall away because of you, I will never fall away.” — Matthew 26:33

But confidence without dependence…
is a setup.

Jesus is arrested.
Chaos erupts.
Fear fills the air like smoke.

Just enough to still feel connected…
without being identified.
We don’t walk away from Jesus.
A servant girl looks at Peter.
“The Lord turned and looked straight at Peter.” — Luke 22:61

And in that look—
Peter saw everything.

His pride.
His fear.
His failure.
“And he went outside and wept bitterly.” — Luke 22:62
This is the part we don’t like to admit:
We are not just the faithful ones in the story.

Every time we stayed silent
when truth needed a voice.

Every time we blended in
to avoid standing out.
Every time we chose approval over obedience.
Every time we lived like we didn’t know Him…
Denial doesn’t always sound like rejection.
It was rooted in something dangerous:

He said,
“Even if everyone else fails… I won’t.”
“Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.” — Proverbs 16:18
Peter didn’t fall because he was weak.
He fell because he thought he was strong.

The moment you think,
“I would never do that…”
You’re already closer than you think.
“Before the rooster crows today, you will deny three times that you know me.” — Luke 22:34
Let that settle in your spirit.

Jesus saw the denial…
and stayed.
Now here’s where the Gospel explodes with beauty.
Because Peter’s story doesn’t end in failure.
We’ve denied God in thought, word, and action.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
And sin separates us from Him.
“The wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
But Jesus didn’t walk away from sinners.
“But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

Jesus took your denial…
and paid for it in blood.

Failure is not final—
if you run back to Jesus.
Repentance is not just feeling bad.
“Lord… I failed. But I still love You.”
Where have you been denying Him?
And He’s still looking at you—
Because the same Jesus who looked at Peter…
And His grace is still enough.
